identity.name: People's Democratic Republic of Yemen
native_names: جمهورية اليمن الديمقراطية الشعبية (Jumhūriyyat al-Yaman ad-Dīmuqrāṭiyya ash-Shaʿbiyya)

land.text: the Federation of South Arabia, one of the two British-protected states the National Liberation Front overthrew on 30 November 1967

predecessors.note: The page names both predecessors in the infobox and does not divide the land between them; no Cliopatria row exists for either.

land.text: the Protectorate of South Arabia, the second predecessor named in the infobox

predecessors.note: Same note: the land is the whole 1969 shape, shared with the Federation.

land.text: all of South Yemen, which 'unified with the Yemen Arab Republic, on 22 May 1990, to form the present-day Republic of Yemen'

successors.note: The union also took North Yemen (north-yemen). Cliopatria's PDRY row ends in 1989 and the Republic of Yemen row starts in 1990; this dossier ends in May 1990.

capitals.name: Aden
capitals.note: 'Its capital and largest city was Aden.' Coordinates from the gazetteer's place list.

rulers.name: Salim Rubaya Ali
rulers.title: President
rulers.note: President from 22 June 1969; the page gives no end year, so 1978 is the year the next entry begins.

rulers.name: Abdul Fattah Ismail
rulers.title: President
rulers.note: Infobox 1978-1980; the text says he resigned in 1980 and went into exile in Moscow.

rulers.name: Ali Nasir Muhammad
rulers.title: President
rulers.note: Infobox 1980-1986; ousted during the civil war of January 1986.

rulers.name: Haidar al-Attas
rulers.note: Infobox 1986-1990; the page does not say what office, and lists Ali Salem al-Beidh for the same years (he became General Secretary of the Yemeni Socialist Party after the 1986 war).

correction.text: the whole of the former Federation and Protectorate of South Arabia: Aden, Hadhramaut, Mahra and the Socotra archipelago

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1967-1968, before Cliopatria's row (1969): the National Liberation Front overthrew the Federation and the Protectorate 'to become the People's Republic of Southern Yemen (PRSY) on 30 November 1967'. The page names Aden, Hadhramaut, Mahra and Socotra as the lands the NLF took, with no date. The shape is the 1969 shape.

313,160 km2 for 1969-1986 against the infobox's 287,490 km2 (ratio 1.09) and the body's 'estimated at 208,106 square kilometres' (ratio 1.50; neither figure has a year). Inside the factor of two. By the gazetteer the shape reaches 4,046 km2 into Oman (52.1-53.1E) and 1,517 km2 into Saudi Arabia (47.3-49.0E): desert frontiers the page does not describe, so they are read as outline noise, not claims. The shape's bbox (43.6-54.4E) leaves out Kamaran, which North Yemen seized in 1972, and Perim.

313,160 km2 for 1987-1989, the same outline as 1969. It holds until the unification of 22 May 1990 ('unified with the Yemen Arab Republic, on 22 May 1990'), a year longer than the Cliopatria row, whose successor row (Republic of Yemen) begins in 1990.

region.text: Aden, Hadhramaut, Mahra and Socotra, the lands the NLF took

ledger.note: 30 November 1967: the People's Republic of Southern Yemen is proclaimed at Aden. The Federation of South Arabia and the Protectorate of South Arabia 'were overthrown to become the People's Republic of Southern Yemen (PRSY) on 30 November 1967'; admitted to the UN on 14 December 1967.

30 November 1970: the state becomes the People's Democratic Republic of Yemen. The National Front 'reorganised the country into the People's Democratic Republic of Yemen (PDRY) on 30 November 1970'; same state, same land.

region.text: Kamaran island in the Red Sea

ledger.note: 1972: North Yemen seizes Kamaran. Perim, Kamaran and the Socotra archipelago were part of the state; Kamaran remained so 'until 1972, when North Yemen seized it'. The same year 'Fighting broke out in 1972, and the short-lived conflict was resolved with negotiations.' Kamaran is smaller than a grid cell and outside the Cliopatria shape.

region.text: all of South Yemen, joining the Yemen Arab Republic

ledger.note: 22 May 1990: South Yemen unites with North Yemen. The state 'unified with the Yemen Arab Republic, on 22 May 1990, to form the present-day Republic of Yemen'.
22 May 1990: the People's Democratic Republic of Yemen ends in the Republic of Yemen (same sentence); its land and North Yemen's make the new state, which Cliopatria draws from 1990.

wars.name: Dhofar Rebellion
wars.outcome: After the leadership change of 1969 the PDRY 'declared support for the Dhofar Revolution' and in 1975 gave 'artillery support against the Omani government'; the page gives no territorial result.
wars.note: The page dates only the 1969 declaration and the 1975 fire; the years in between are not on it. Listed so the reviewer sees it was considered.

wars.name: North Yemen-South Yemen fighting of 1972

zones.text: Kamaran island, seized by North Yemen

wars.outcome: 'Fighting broke out in 1972, and the short-lived conflict was resolved with negotiations'; North Yemen seized Kamaran in 1972.
wars.note: Title chosen from the page's sentence (no separate article was opened); the page does not call it a border war or say where it was fought.

wars.name: Second Yemenite War
wars.outcome: Plans for unity were 'put on hold in 1979, as the PDRY funded Red rebels in the YAR'; an Arab League intervention ended the war. The page names no territory.
wars.note: The page calls this the Second Yemenite War.

wars.name: South Yemen Civil War
wars.outcome: The civil war began in Aden on 13 January 1986, 'lasted for more than a month and resulted in thousands of casualties'; Ali Nasir Muhammad was ousted and Ali Salem al-Beidh became General Secretary of the Yemeni Socialist Party.
wars.note: A fight inside the ruling party, with no change of border.

certainty.note: Judgment, not read from a page: the frontiers with Saudi Arabia and Oman ran through desert and were not demarcated in these years; the page describes no frontier treaty. The coast and the border with North Yemen (fought over in 1972 and 1979) are firmer.

sources.title: South Yemen
sources.note: The only page opened (budget 1-2): infobox area 287,490 km2 and capital, 30 November 1967 and 1970, Kamaran 1972, the wars of 1972, 1979 and 1986, Dhofar, 22 May 1990, the rulers.

notes: Written by me-10-l on 2026-10-25 from one page (the Wikipedia article 'South Yemen'). SHARED WIKIDATA Q199841 with republic-of-yemen: treated as DIFFERENT states. The PDRY ended on 22 May 1990 in the merger; the Republic of Yemen (Cliopatria 1990-2024, dossier by another me-10 part, whose predecessors list this slug) is the union of it and North Yemen. The colour agent may still keep one hue for the south of the union. ROW BOUNDARIES: Cliopatria's row runs 1969-1989 and begins two years after the state (30 November 1967): new keyframe 1967-1968. The dossier ends in May 1990, one year past the row, which leaves 1990 shared with the Republic of Yemen row. PREDECESSORS: the Federation of South Arabia and the Protectorate of South Arabia (and the Aden Colony before them) have no Cliopatria row and no dossier; a gap-filler should write them (not opened). SHAPE: 313,160 km2 against 287,490 km2 (infobox) and 208,106 km2 (body); the shape runs 4,046 km2 into Oman and 1,517 km2 into Saudi Arabia by the gazetteer, and omits Kamaran and Perim. PAGE SILENT: the Yemeni-Saudi and Yemeni-Omani frontiers, Saudi-backed border clashes, the dates between 1969 and 1975 of the Dhofar support, the location of the 1972 and 1979 fighting. NAMES FOR THE GAZETTEER: Kamaran (place).
